Maria: Heads-up: I'm drafting an operator UX for partial payload resume + backpressure when fetching airgapped bundles. Quick read-through?

Kevin: Yep — low-level Q: how do we detect partial fetch vs corrupted blob? We already have manifest checksums, but want to be explicit.

Maria: Plan: fetcher writes incremental chunks to a .tmp file and maintains a chunk-index. On interruption we keep last-verified-chunk and resume from next chunk. Final step: manifest-level Merkle verify before marking verified. Backpressure via token-bucket per-operator to limit concurrent chunk fetches.

Raj: Sounds reasonable. Edge case: apply needs atomic activation. If we allow partial downloads to sit around, operator should move objects to a quarantine namespace until fully verified, otherwise activation must fail.

Alice: API-wise I'd expose statuses: downloading, partial, verified, quarantined, ready-to-activate. Also add `spec.resumePolicy: partial | restart` so operators can opt into restart-only for very strict environments.

Sarah: Partial resume is helpful but for model shards we should prefer range requests and chunk dedupe. In some airgap setups the transfer appliance doesn't support HTTP range — we need a small adapter or fallback to whole-file transfers.

Kevin: Also concerned about disk pressure. If N packages are partially fetched concurrently we risk filling ephemeral storage. Suggest controller-level knobs: `maxPartialBytes`, `maxPartialFiles`, and a global inflight limit with eviction LRU.

OpsBot: deploy-checker: manifest signature OK, agent-version compatible with resume protocol v1.

Maria: Proposed operator config (sketch):
```yaml
controller:
  concurrency: 4 # concurrent bundle downloads per node
  resumePolicy: partial # partial|restart
  backpressure:
    tokenBucket:
      rate: 4 # chunks/sec
      burst: 8
  storage:
    maxPartialBytes: 10737418240 # 10Gi
    partialRetentionDays: 30
```

Raj: One more thought: if manifest is content-addressed we can avoid per-chunk signatures, but we MUST record chunk hashes during download so resume can validate each chunk. That prevents silent corruption when resuming.

Alice: UX: `rctl package resume <package-id>` for ops. Reconcile loop should auto-clean partials older than `partialRetentionDays` or when global disk pressure high. Document as operator best-practice.

Kevin: I'll add this to the RFC follow-up doc and propose metrics to track: `partial_retries_total`, `resume_success_rate`, `partial_disk_exhaustion_count`, `partial_cleanup_count`.

Maria: Nice. I'll push a small PR with CRD patches + controller sketch and tag you all. Quick ask: anybody oppose adding `resumePolicy` to CRD?

Raj: No objections. Fine to iterate.

Sarah: +1. Will add a note about fallbacks when range requests aren't available.

Alice: +1 — can we also include operator logs that surface "bytes_reserved" and "active_partials" for support debugging?

Maria: Good call — adding those fields to the controller status. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
